match.reason: The bank point covers the basic favourable-over-total probability rule but not counting arrangements with the multiplication principle, which is the core idea of the new point, so it is related rather than the same idea.

draft.title: Probability by counting arrangements
card: When every arrangement is equally likely, the probability of an event is \(\frac{\text{favourable arrangements}}{\text{all arrangements}}\). Both numbers can be found by counting.

Count all the arrangements first. Use the multiplication principle: multiply the number of ways to fill each place. A 3-digit code from the digits 1 to 5, with no digit repeated, has \(5 \times 4 \times 3 = 60\) arrangements.

Then count the favourable arrangements the same way. Fill the most restricted place first. Codes that end in 5: the last place has 1 way, then \(4 \times 3\) for the first two, giving \(4 \times 3 \times 1 = 12\).
Divide favourable by all. The probability that the code ends in 5 is \(\frac{12}{60} = \frac{1}{5}\).
draft.remember: Count the favourable arrangements and all the arrangements with the multiplication principle, then divide.

a.q: A 3-digit code uses the digits 1 to 5, with no digit repeated. Each code is equally likely. What is the probability that it starts with 2?
a.why: Starting with 2 leaves 4 digits for the second place and 3 for the third, so \(1 \times 4 \times 3 = 12\) favourable codes out of \(5 \times 4 \times 3 = 60\). The option with 125 wrongly lets digits repeat in the total.
a.clue: Fix the first place, then count the ways to fill the other two.

b.q: Mia makes a 4-digit PIN from the digits 1 to 6, with no digit repeated. Each PIN is equally likely. What is the probability that it is even?
b.why: All PINs: \(6 \times 5 \times 4 \times 3 = 360\). Even PINs: the last place has 3 ways (2, 4 or 6), then \(5 \times 4 \times 3 = 60\) for the rest, giving 180. So \(\frac{180}{360} = \frac{1}{2}\). Using 1 way for the last place gives \(\frac{1}{6}\), which is the chance of one particular ending digit.
b.clue: Fill the last place first, then count what remains for the others.
